Not reproduced on B200: output identical on 300,000 launches with TMEM scrubbed before each. One thread issues `tcgen05.cp` (sparsity metadata) and then `tcgen05.mma.sp`, which reads the metadata at a TMEM address other than the copy destination; PTX 9.4 guarantees pipeline order for this pair only at the same address
PTX version interpretation (2026-10-12): the corpus declares PTX 9.2, whose documentation guarantees pipelined tcgen05.cp -> tcgen05.mma ordering for the same cta_group N without an address condition. PTX 9.4 requires same N and address for non-4x256b copies; the current verifier follows the latter interpretation and rejects this copy-base-before-MMA-subregion case. Shape restrictions belong to separate MMA -> MMA rules, not this cp -> MMA rule. Whether 9.4 corrects prior documentation or changes the guarantee remains unconfirmed; disposition unresolved. [PTX 9.2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#tcgen05-memory-consistency-model-pipelined-instructions), [PTX 9.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#tcgen05-memory-consistency-model-pipelined-instructions).

Benign on B200: duplicate same-value stores (two store sites, all writers agree); output identical on 300,000 launches ([#50](https://github.com/wmdi/wasp_verification/issues/50))

Source analysis (2026-10-12): suspected kernel synchronization gap, not confirmed. The original write_o_reg_gmem path performs stmatrix followed by cross-lane shared-memory reads without an explicit warp memory barrier between them; stmatrix.sync.aligned is a weak memory operation, so the qualifiers alone do not establish the required memory ordering. Further collective-access analysis is needed to rule out a verifier modeling gap. No new B200 test was run for this source analysis. [Pinned source](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/8c94f70f49fbe17adb5deae5b2b48ff467346863/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L2219-L2260).

Race reproduced on B200, not a kernel bug: two output elements are each written by two threads with different values (which one is kept did not vary in 300,000 launches). Overlapping output memory is a documented PyTorch limitation ([#48](https://github.com/wmdi/wasp_verification/issues/48))

Bug: reproduced on B200. Delaying warp 0's copy into `A_shared` by 2 µs changes the output on 52% of launches, by 20 µs or more on over 99.9%; a 500 µs delay before the copies of the race-free sibling kernels changes nothing. Without the delay the output is identical on 300,000 launches and matches a host-computed GEMM

Compiler bug (source analysis, 2026-10-12); not tested on B200. Generated PTX invalidates pipeline mbarriers before the final MMA-completion wait, without establishing completion of outstanding asynchronous notifications. LowerAref inserts cleanup after the last IR user rather than proven asynchronous completion. branch_decisions.note: vectorize_read_with_alignment<16>: the token's input row pointer is 32-byte aligned (PyTorch allocations are 256-byte aligned and the 2048-byte row stride keeps every row aligned), so the vectorized path is taken instead of the scalar fallback. User-authorized scenario; the frontend cannot decide alignment of a symbolic pointer.

vectorize_with_alignment<16>: the token's input row (32-byte aligned) and fp8 output row (16-byte aligned) allow the vectorized quantization path; the scalar fallback is not taken. User-authorized scenario; the frontend cannot decide alignment of symbolic pointers.
